question: Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste introduces key obligations to ensure that producers help pay for the management of packaging waste. However, the application of Articles 44 and 45 risks creating a disproportionate administrative burden for tradespeople and micro and small enterprises involved in cross-border B2C online trade. 1.

Does the Commission intend to perform a targeted assessment of the impact of Articles 44 and 45 on tradespeople and micro and small enterprises occasionally selling crossborder B2C or placing very small quantities of packaging on the market of another Member State, encompassing cumulative fixed administrative costs in more than one Member States?

How does it intend to ensure that registration fees and the costs associated with mandatory authorised representation are proportionate and based on actual costs, particularly for producers placing very small quantities of packaging on the market of a single Member State?

Is it considering the possibility of establishing a harmonised, simplified regime or a de minimis threshold for very small quantities of packaging and occasional cross-border sales, as well as a single European registration and reporting system, modelled on the VAT One Stop Shop scheme, while maintaining the obligation on producers to help pay for the management of packaging waste in the country of destination?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) The priority of the Commission is to make the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1 work in practice. The PPWR will help reduce packaging waste and improve recycling and the functioning of the Single Market by creating a harmonised set of rules that apply in all Member States.
The PPWR introduces key obligations to ensure that producers help pay for the management of packaging waste. This is crucial to manage effectively the generated packaging waste in the EU.

The application of Articles 44 and 45 and the future implementing act under Article 44(14) will take into account the Commission priority on simplification and reducing administrative burden for companies, notably small and medium-sized companies.

To address the recent concerns, the Commission proposed, in December 2025, in its Environmental Omnibus2, to suspend the obligation for producers to appoint an authorised representative when they sell packaged products directly to consumers in Member States other than the one where they are located. The proposal is currently being examined by the European Parliament and the Council.

While the suspension proposal is being negotiated, the Commission is encouraging the Member States to have a pragmatic enforcement As part of the work on the upcoming proposal for a Circular Economy Act, the Commission is looking more broadly at how Extended Producer Responsibility schemes can be improved focusing on simplification, harmonisation and digitalisation, using the full potential of the Single Market.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/simplification-administrative-burdens-environmentallegislation_en.
